recordings.remarks: This is a single adult male lyrebird producing mimetic song while standing on the ground under some shrubs in a dense sclerophyll forest on a sunny day. Other lyrebirds can be heard very faintly in the distance and there were no other species vocalizing in background. The bird was recorded from approximately 10 meters away, it was not located on a display mound, and it walked off to another location while making the click sounds starting at 1:49 . The "walking while clicking behavior" is a way they lead another lyrebird to follow them to their display mound.
recordings.carol_category: mimetic song (adult male on the ground; 'click' walking sounds from 1:49)

recordings.location: Sherbrooke Forest, Yarra Ranges, Victoria, Australia
recordings.remarks:
In Woi wurrung, the language of the Wurundjeri people, the Traditional Owners of this part of outer Melbourne, Superb Lyrebirds are known as Buln Buln and are understood as multi-linguists rather than mimics. 

 With the expert guidance of Jan Incoll from the Sherbrooke Lyrebird Study Group, this is a recording of the song of a male Superb Lyrebird in Sherbrooke Forest, and an answering/responsive song can be heard in the distance. The bird allowed us to get remarkably near. His song includes renditions of Eastern Whipbird, Black Cockatoo, Laughing Kookaburra, Red Wattlebird, Common Blackbird, Pied Currawong plus the Lyrebird’s own call. This is the mating season for the birds, very early Spring. Cool temperate rainforest dominated by Mountain Ash and tree ferns. Rich dense undergrowth. Cold and windy. 

 Translation kindly provided by Wurundjeri artist and linguist Mandy Nicholson.
recordings.carol_category: male song with mimicry (Sherbrooke; answering song in the distance)
recordings.attribution: XC492308 by Catherine Clover, xeno-canto.org/492308, Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0

recordings.remarks:
Single male superb lyrebird singing between sessions of feeding on invertebrates recovered from beneath overturned leaf litter. Corymbia eximia and eucalyptis punctata forest with acacia, persoonia, hakea and banksia under storey. Deep leaf litter layer. 

 The performance includes imitative fragments of other local species including noisy friarbird, currawong, kookaburra, crimson rosella. 

 Sunny. Forest exceedingly damp as floodwaters recede after record rains in preceding weeks.
recordings.carol_category: mimetic song + alarm calls (single male between feeding bouts)
